---
title: "Step 4. What your level requires"
description: "The checks your level asks for, phase by phase."
---

Do what your level requires, from the phase you are in to Phase 4. Get your level from [Step 3, read your level](read-your-level.qmd). You get it at design, so start with the Phase 2 table.

**Do everything in the column for your level and in the columns for the levels below it.**

If an impact dimension scored 4, go to [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd).

## What each phase requires

Use the table for the phase you are in. In these tables the assurer and the reviewer are your critical friend.

### In Phase 1, engagement and scoping

| Task | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 3 Comprehensive |
|-------------|--------------------------|------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| **Commission and frame** | Commissioner states the decision and the deadline. You confirm your understanding in writing, however briefly. An email is enough | The commissioning conversation is recorded: the decision, the question, what is out of scope, and the quality expected | Formal commissioning record. Business Critical status considered explicitly and recorded either way. Where it is Business Critical, the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer is named and aware |
| **Score the impact** | You score it and record it in your project record | You and the commissioner agree it together. Disagreement goes to the Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead | The Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead confirms it. Register entry where Business Critical |

: Phase 1 tasks and what each assurance level requires for them

At every level you may reframe a request that arrives as an output rather than a question.
Challenge any request that needs it.

### In Phase 2, design

| Task | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 3 Comprehensive |
|--------------|-------------------|---------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| **Score the likelihood and finish the level** | You score it once the data and the method are settled, and write the level into the specification | As Level 1, and you and the commissioner agree the finished level | As Level 1, and the Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead confirms the finished level |
| **Plan the assurance** | Note your method and main assumptions. No separate assurance plan | An assurance plan: who reviews, what, and when. **The reviewer is named before work starts** | Assurance plan agreed with an assurer from outside your team. Verification and validation activities specified |
| **Book the time** | Allow for the colleague check | Assurer's time in the schedule, agreed with them | Assurer's time agreed and protected. Re-review time allowed for |
| **Check the design before work starts** | Not required | A critical friend confirms the approach answers the question and the assurance planned is right. Commissioner approves the design before work proceeds | As Level 2, with the assurer from outside the team |

: Phase 2 tasks and what each assurance level requires for them

#### Find a critical friend

These are recommended, not required.

- Assign a critical friend early, ideally while you are still defining the problem.
- Choose someone with experience of similar data or techniques. If you are the area expert, consider a newer colleague.
- Ask your team lead first. Contact the Data Science team or the Data Science Lead if you need a recommendation.
- Involve them throughout the work, not only at the end.

::: {.nhsuk-inset-text}
More detail: [how to find and work with a critical friend](/guidance/09-resources/r17-roles-independence-and-escalation.qmd#naming-and-working-with-the-critical-friend).
:::

### In Phase 3, analysis

| Task | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 3 Comprehensive |
|------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------------------|
| **Produce** | Keep inputs and working reproducible enough that someone else could re-run it | Work under version control. Log decisions and assumption changes as they happen | Maintain an assumptions register. Plan sensitivity testing at design stage, not afterwards |
| **Quality assure** | Self-check against the Level 1 checks. A colleague sense checks your headline numbers | **Independent peer review by someone outside the work.** Code review where scripted. Quality assurance log completed and retained | Full verification and validation. Code assured. Uncertainty documented and quantified where the method allows |

: Phase 3 tasks and what each assurance level requires for them

Where your analysis involves code, follow the
[NHSBSA Analytical Code Assurance Playbook](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-analytical-code-assurance-playbook).

Make the analysis reproducible, with automation that suits its complexity. See
[reproducible and automated analysis compared](/guidance/09-resources/r9-what-each-standard-asks-for.qmd#reproducible-and-automated-analysis-compared).

### In Phase 4, delivery and sign-off

| Task | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 3 Comprehensive |
|-------------|--------------------------|---------------------------------|----------------------------|
| **Communicate** | State your main limitation alongside the result. A short quality assurance statement required | Quality assurance statement required. Caveats, limitations and uncertainty stated **in the output itself, not only in an annex** | Statement published with the output. Uncertainty ranges communicated |
| **Sign off and archive** | Store the project record with the output. No formal sign-off beyond you | **Signed off by your team lead.** Project record, quality assurance log and code archived together and linked from the output | Signed off by the Lead Official for Statistics. Register updated. Review date set |

: Phase 4 tasks and what each assurance level requires for them

Every level needs a quality assurance statement before sign-off. It covers assumptions,
uncertainty, limitations, and what the results can and cannot be used for. See
[the quality assurance statement, with a worked example](../09-resources/r5-quality-assurance-statement.qmd).

## What to record

Complete the sections of the project record that your level requires.

| Section of the project record | Level 1 | Level 2 | Level 3 |
|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------|---------------|---------------|
| 1. Header: title, reference, level, analyst, commissioner, dates, Business Critical yes or no | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| 2. The question: the decision it supports, the question, what is out of scope, the deadline | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| 3. Data: source, owner, extract date, known quality issues, effect on the analysis, access basis | Not required | Yes | Yes |
| 4. Method: approach, why this and not the alternatives, tools and code repository | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| 5. Assumptions: assumption, rationale, impact if wrong, sensitivity tested, agreed with | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| 6. Uncertainty: principal sources, how quantified or why not, how communicated | Not required | Yes | Yes, quantified |
| 7. Decision log, including **deviations from the plan** | Not required | Yes | Yes |
| 8. Assurance and sign-off: role, name, date, what they confirmed | Not required | Yes | Yes, plus approver |
| 9. **Lessons learned** | Not required | Yes | Yes |

: Sections of the project record, and whether each level needs them

At Level 1, complete the rows marked Yes in the Level 1 column only. That is about one side of A4.

- Identify relevant lessons from earlier work when you plan, and capture new lessons as you go.
- Keep records version controlled, securely stored and retrievable.
- Hold the project record on the NHSBSA SharePoint, in the same place as the output it documents.

## The checks, by level

Do every check first required at your level or at a lower level. From Level 2, record in your
quality assurance log each check you did, when, what you found and the conclusion you drew.

| First required at | Check | What that means here |
|---|---|---|
| **Level 1** | Validation of requirements | You confirm the question, the decision it informs and what is out of scope, in writing with the commissioner |
| **Level 1** | Specification, user guide and notes | Enough written down that someone else could pick the work up. At this level it is short |
| **Level 1** | Data sources and assumptions clear | Source, extract date and provenance recorded. Assumptions listed with the rationale and the effect if wrong. Known data quality issues named, with their effect stated |
| **Level 1** | Accuracy of data transformations and calculations | You check your own transformations and totals. A colleague sense checks the headline numbers |
| **Level 1** | Methodological correctness | You document the method, with the alternatives you considered and why you did not use them |
| **Level 1** | Sense checking results | Outputs compared against an independent reference: last period, a related series, or an order-of-magnitude expectation |
| **Level 1** | Clarity, accessibility and security of outputs | Limitations stated in the output itself rather than only in an annex. Accessible format. Handled at the right classification |
| **Level 2** | Responsibilities and accountabilities | The analyst, the reviewer and the approver are named before the work starts |
| **Level 2** | Appropriateness of methodology | Someone who had no hand in the work agrees the method answers the question |
| **Level 2** | Documentation and audit trails | You complete the quality assurance log as you go, and keep it with the analysis |
| **Level 2** | Understanding of the impacts of data quality | Input data profiled: ranges, nulls, duplicates, outliers, and what each means for the answer.<br><br>**Including who is missing from it**: treat a gap in coverage as a blind spot in the conclusion. It is a risk of affecting one group differently |
| **Level 2** | Evidence based assumptions | Each assumption is traceable to a source, a precedent or a stated expert judgement |
| **Level 2** | Code scrutiny | Code peer reviewed and version controlled |
| **Level 2** | Validation with stakeholders and subject matter experts | The people who know the business area see the results before release and say whether they are plausible |
| **Level 2** | Sensitivity testing | Key assumptions varied to see whether the conclusion moves. Where material at this level |
| **Level 2** | Triangulation and independent validation of results | Calculations independently reproduced from source by the reviewer |
| **Level 3** | Change control processes | You record any change to data, method or code after sign-off, and re-assure it proportionately |
| **Level 3** | Ethical risks | Assessed against the Data and AI Ethics Framework, per [data ethics and personal data](../09-resources/r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd) |
| **Level 3** | Knowledge sharing | The method and the lessons are shared beyond the delivering team |
| **Level 3** | Detailed documentation review | The assurer reads the documentation as a document, not only the numbers |
| **Level 3** | Usability testing | The output is tested with someone who will use it, not only with someone who made it |
| **Level 3** | Automated checks | Validation built into the pipeline so it runs every time rather than once |
| **Level 3** | Additional scenario testing | Behaviour under plausible alternative inputs, not just the expected ones |
| **Level 3** | Independent peer review | An assurer from outside the delivering team. Code assured against the [NHSBSA Analytical Code Assurance Playbook](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-analytical-code-assurance-playbook). Uncertainty quantified where the method allows. Quality assurance statement published with the output |
| **Level 4 BCA** | Formal audits | See [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd) |
| **Level 4 BCA** | External review | As above |
| **Level 4 BCA** | Additional scrutiny of documentation | As above |
| **Level 4 BCA** | Scrutiny of structural and conceptual assumptions | As above |
| **Level 4 BCA** | Additional scenario testing | As above |

: Each check, the level that first requires it, and what it means here

Check at scoping whether the Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard applies, whatever your
level. It does if a tool:

- has a significant influence on a decision-making process with public effect, or
- interacts directly with the general public.

::: {.nhsuk-inset-text}
More detail: [the transparency record test](/guidance/09-resources/r12-algorithmic-transparency-and-ai.qmd#check-whether-your-tool-needs-a-transparency-record).
:::
